page: Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the c3 server family. It is configured with 4 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs, mapped from 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8481C processor operating at 2.7 GHz. The system includes 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It features an L3 cache size of 105 MB and supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE, AMX_INT8) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512). This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators.

Performance benchmarks reveal a divergence between single-core and multi-core execution. Single-core metrics, such as the stress-ng single-core CPU performance of 1618.89 and Geekbench single-core score of 1713.0, rank in the average tier. However, multi-core benchmarks, including the stress-ng multi-core score of 3315.66 and Geekbench multi-core score of 3813.0, fall into the weak category. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with uncached large-block read speeds at 28.42 GB/sec and write speeds at 21.13 GB/sec, both placing in the bottom 25% of tested hardware.

The qualitative cost profile of the c3-standard-4 reflects its position as a dedicated-resource entry point. While the inclusion of AMX and AVX-512 instructions provides hardware-level acceleration for specific cryptographic and vector operations, the low multi-threaded scaling and restricted memory bandwidth present a clear tradeoff. This instance is suited for workloads that rely on single-threaded efficiency or moderate compute requirements, such as static web serving, basic text processing, and lightweight single-threaded compression tasks. It is less suited for memory-intensive database operations, software compilation, or parallelized multi-threaded processing.
description: The Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-4 is an x86_64 virtual machine featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8481C processor running at 2.7 GHz, paired with 16.0 GB of RAM. It lacks local storage and GPU accelerators but includes advanced hardware features like Intel AMX and AVX-512. Benchmark data indicates average single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1713.0 and steady static web serving throughput of 6.68 GB/sec. However, multi-core performance and memory bandwidth are relatively weak, as shown by a multi-core Geekbench score of 3813.0 and uncached read speeds of 28.42 GB/sec. This resource profile makes the instance best suited for single-threaded applications, lightweight web serving, and basic text processing, while presenting a clear performance tradeoff for highly parallelized or memory-bound workloads.
